Mountain Capital Investment Advisors Inc increased its stake in Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 34.8% during the third quarter, Holdings Channel reports. The fund owned 8,850 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after buying an additional 2,285 shares during the period. Apple makes up approximately 1.2% of Mountain Capital Investment Advisors Inc’s holdings, making the stock its 12th biggest position. Mountain Capital Investment Advisors Inc’s holdings in Apple were worth $1,364,000 as of its most recent filing with the Securities & Exchange Commission. 
Several other hedge funds and other institutional investors also recently modified their holdings of AAPL. Pennsylvania Trust Co boosted its position in Apple by 34.7% during the second quarter. Pennsylvania Trust Co now owns 314,298 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $45,265,000 after purchasing an additional 80,898 shares during the last quarter. Stokes & Hubbell Capital Management LLC boosted its position in Apple by 2.3% during the second quarter. Stokes & Hubbell Capital Management LLC now owns 48,594 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $6,999,000 after purchasing an additional 1,111 shares during the last quarter. Burke & Herbert Bank & Trust Co. boosted its position in Apple by 0.8% during the second quarter. Burke & Herbert Bank & Trust Co. now owns 20,928 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $3,014,000 after purchasing an additional 173 shares during the last quarter. CHURCHILL MANAGEMENT Corp boosted its position in Apple by 107.4% during the second quarter. CHURCHILL MANAGEMENT Corp now owns 38,990 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $5,615,000 after purchasing an additional 20,190 shares during the last quarter. Finally, Arvest Bank Trust Division boosted its position in Apple by 1.1% during the second quarter. Arvest Bank Trust Division now owns 224,853 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $32,384,000 after purchasing an additional 2,480 shares during the last quarter. In other Apple news, insider Eduardo H. Cue sold 65,361 shares of the company’s stock in a transaction on Thursday, November 30th. The stock was sold at an average price of $171.60, for a total transaction of $11,215,947.60. The transaction was disclosed in a filing with the SEC, which is available at this link . Also, SVP Johny Srouji sold 5,760 shares of the company’s stock in a transaction on Wednesday, November 22nd. The stock was sold at an average price of $174.40, for a total value of $1,004,544.00. Following the transaction, the senior vice president now directly owns 81,560 shares in the company, valued at approximately $14,224,064. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . Over the last quarter, insiders sold 128,412 shares of company stock worth $22,115,155. Corporate insiders own 0.08% of the company’s stock. Shares of Apple Inc. ( NASDAQ AAPL ) opened at $167.43 on Thursday. Apple Inc. has a 12 month low of $120.62 and a 12 month high of $180.10. The firm has a market capitalization of $849,385.69, a P/E ratio of 18.20, a PEG ratio of 1.35 and a beta of 1.21. The company has a quick ratio of 1.23, a current ratio of 1.28 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.73. 
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last released its quarterly earnings data on Thursday, November 2nd. The iPhone maker reported $2.07 earnings per share for the quarter, beating the consensus estimate of $1.87 by $0.20. Apple had a return on equity of 36.29% and a net margin of 21.09%. The company had revenue of $52.58 billion for the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $50.71 billion. During the same period in the prior year, the company posted $1.50 EPS. The company’s revenue was up 12.2% compared to the same quarter last year. sell-side analysts predict that Apple Inc. will post 11.13 earnings per share for the current year. 
A number of research firms have recently commented on AAPL. Macquarie set a $188.00 price objective on Apple and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a research note on Friday, January 26th. ValuEngine upgraded Apple from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating in a research note on Sunday, December 31st. Zacks Investment Research upgraded Apple from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating and set a $197.00 price objective on the stock in a research note on Thursday, January 18th. Piper Jaffray Companies reiterated a “buy” rating and issued a $200.00 price objective on shares of Apple in a research note on Tuesday, January 2nd. Finally, Bank of America lowered Apple from a “buy” rating to a “neutral” rating and lifted their price objective for the stock from $180.00 to $220.00 in a research note on Wednesday, January 17th. Two research analysts have rated the stock with a sell rating, twelve have given a hold rating, thirty-seven have assigned a buy rating and two have issued a strong buy rating to the company’s stock. Apple presently has an average rating of “Buy” and an average target price of $201.25.
